label: Maya, then the problem
show: Night stage. 'Maya, 16'. Three lines (Plans, Sleep, Texts) run level, then each slips amber as it is named. A quote: 'It's just finals.' Then '2 months' before anyone asked. Then five dots, one amber: 1 in 5. Then a bar: 59% get no treatment. Then 'nobody knows when to ask.'
text: Maya is sixteen. Last fall she quit soccer. By December she slept five hours a night and texted her friends half as much. Her mom thought it was finals, but two months passed before anyone asked her how she really was. Maya is one of many: one in five US teens has depression each year, and fifty-nine percent get no treatment. Nobody knows when to really ask.

label: What we built
show: The Stability mark draws itself. Two phones slide in, Maya's and her mom's, linked by a dotted line.
text: So we built Stability: an app on Maya's phone, linked to her mom's, that knows when to ask.

label: Her digital life, with consent
show: Two chips: 'Maya agreed', 'Mom agreed'. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, browsing and news feeds light up on the left; Spotify, games and chats on the right under '17 sources'. A line: parents never see a message, search or video. Then Stable floats in and settles into the check-in card.
text: With consent from Maya and her parents, it connects to her digital life: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, browsing, newsfeeds, Spotify, games and chats. It's all read on her phone, and her parents never see a message, search or video. Once a week, our mascot Stable checks in: two taps.

label: It asks, and asks early
show: Week 4: the two questions; she answers 'several days' to both, 2 of 6. Weeks 5 and 6: the ring turns amber, her check-in stress goes from 2 to 4, the ask model's score climbs from 0.05 past 0.16, and the questions come up again in week 6.
text: Every month, Stable asks the two screening questions doctors use. In week four, Maya scores two of six. During finals, her stress check-ins jump from two to four, and our ask model asks again two weeks early.

label: The note
show: Week 8: she scores 4 of 6, so all eight questions come up; total 12. Maya sees a doctor nudge. Mom's phone slides in; an amber dot crosses; chips: Sleep and messaging down, For 4 weeks, How to start the talk. 'Never her messages.'
text: In week eight she scores four, so all eight questions come up: twelve, past the cutoff of ten. Maya is nudged to see a doctor, and her mom gets a note: sleep and messaging down for four weeks, and how to start the conversation. Never her messages.

label: Private, with a safety net
show: Maya types a message. It becomes a single dot. A counter holds at 0 bytes sent. A chip: 988, one tap away.
text: Small models read what she types, watches and searches, keep only numbers and delete the words. If she types about self-harm, 988 is one tap away.

label: The engine
show: A diagram builds: two taps and past answers feed the ask model, a logistic regression; past 16% it asks; 2 questions, then all 8 at 3 or more, then a note at 10 or more. Below: her digital life feeds the mood, self-harm and music models, all on the phone.
text: Under the hood, her two taps and past answers feed our ask model, a logistic regression scoring the chance her next screening is high. Past sixteen percent, it asks. Three or more unlocks all eight; ten or more alerts a parent.

label: It works
show: A counter runs to 404,376, broken down: 282,768 posts, 54,263 comments, 30,346 surveyed teens, 16,886 student-weeks and more. Tiles: 3.4x (44% vs 13%), AUC 0.90 on 113 teens, 54% vs 24% for sleep, 2x a keyword list with 13 of 15 self-harm messages.
text: Does it work? We tested on four hundred thousand labelled examples. Our ask model finds a hard week three times as often as a schedule. On a hundred thirteen teens it never saw, its AUC was point nine oh. Teens sleeping four hours or less were twice as likely to feel hopeless.

label: Close
show: The Stability mark, 'knowing when to ask', Stable, and a small 'Prototype. Not medical advice.'
text: Stability. Knowing when to ask, so more teens like Maya get help sooner.
